card.name: Days or drug before a comma or followed-by
card.fires_on: The word "days" ending a dosing duration (e.g. "21 consecutive days", "1 to 3 days"), "day" after "per", and "drug" in "discontinue the drug". The next token is usually a comma or "followed by".

modes.label: Duration in days
modes.description: "days" or "day" closing a dosing schedule phrase.

modes.label: The instruction to discontinue the drug
modes.description: "drug" at the end of the nursing-mother phrase about stopping nursing or the drug.
modes.example: a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the<< drug>> taking into account the importance of the drug

modes.label: Other word endings
modes.description: Occasional non-drug text where a noun ends a clause.
modes.example: placed on the buo<<ys>> at 20-cm depth minus

card.writes: It favors a comma or punctuation next, and suppresses descriptive words like flattened or skewed.
card.plain: It responds to the end of a dosing duration or a "the drug" phrase, where a comma or "followed by" comes next.
